title: C-O5 fix round 1: concrete protected creds path, external home network, mounted repos/pool config, guarded env vars, runbook order, platform pin and checksums, work dir ownership, tighter .dockerignore, container hardening (from security review T-0171)
spec:
Fix round for T-0165 (branch task/T-0165 at c1155c4). Work in this task's worktree, cut from task/T-0165. Security review T-0171 (opus) requested changes; items come from it. Scope: Dockerfile, docker-compose.executor.yml, .dockerignore, docs/executor-host.md, .orchestrator/protected-paths.txt.

1 HIGH protected-paths.txt: guardrails.sh expands `~` only, never `${VAR}`, so `${ORCH_CREDS}` is inert. Replace it with the concrete default `~/orch-creds` and make the runbook and compose use that same default (`ORCH_CREDS=${ORCH_CREDS:-$HOME/orch-creds}` in the runbook; the runbook says: if you choose another root, add it to protected-paths.txt too). Keep the four /home/orch/... lines.

2 HIGH compose networking: add `networks: {default: {external: true, name: "${ORCH_NET:?set ORCH_NET to the docker network the kgpt module runs on}"}}` so the service joins the existing home network; runbook step: find it with `docker network ls` on the kgpt host (the kgpt compose project's default network) and export ORCH_NET before `up`. Still no `ports:`.

3 HIGH config location: serve.py reads repos.toml at /opt/orchestrator/.orchestrator/repos.toml and install/goals.start copies the orchestrator's own .orchestrator/pool.toml into a freshly cloned target. Mount both from the host: `./config/repos.toml:/opt/orchestrator/.orchestrator/repos.toml:ro` and `./config/pool.toml:/opt/orchestrator/.orchestrator/pool.toml:ro`. Runbook step: create ./config/ from .orchestrator/repos.toml.example and the repo's pool.toml, edit there (oauth_token_env, secrets in env: form, repos entries), and `docker compose restart` after edits; explain that an already-installed target repo keeps its own committed .orchestrator/pool.toml and is changed via a PR on that repo, not on the host.

4 MED compose: every `${VAR}` used for mounts gets a `:?message` guard (ORCH_CREDS, ORCH_NET) or a default (UID/GID default 1000). Put `env_file: [{path: ./executor.env, required: true}]` and fix the runbook ORDER so executor.env is created (from a documented template listing the variable names only) BEFORE any `docker compose run` step.

5 MED Dockerfile: `FROM --platform=linux/amd64 ubuntu:24.04@sha256:<digest>` (look up the current digest with `docker buildx imagetools inspect ubuntu:24.04` and record how to bump it in a comment) and select the codex asset from `dpkg --print-architecture` like the gh apt line does, failing the build on an unsupported arch. Note in the runbook that the smoke build on the laptop is arm64-emulated or use `--platform linux/amd64`.

6 MED Dockerfile integrity: verify the codex tarball against the release's published checksum file when the release provides one (check the openai/codex release assets for a .sha256 or checksums file; download it and `sha256sum -c`); if the release publishes none, add `ARG CODEX_SHA256` with the pinned asset's sha256 and verify it. For uv and Claude Code, download the installer scripts to a file first and record their sha256 in the build log (`sha256sum`) before executing; if the vendors publish checksums, verify against them. Say in a Dockerfile comment which of the three are verified and which are only pinned.

7 MED runbook and compose: `./work` (and `./config`) must be created and chowned to the build uid in step 2 alongside the credential dirs; compose mounts `./work:/work`.

8 MED .dockerignore: add `.git`, `.mcp*.json`, `.orchestrator/pool_state.json`, `.orchestrator/memory`, `.orchestrator/tasks`, `.orchestrator/scorecard.json`, `.orchestrator/bench.json`, `.orchestrator/*.lock`, `executor.env`, `config/`. `uv sync --frozen` must still work (it needs pyproject.toml, uv.lock and the package, not .git).

9 LOW compose hardening: `security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]`, `cap_drop: ["ALL"]`, `mem_limit` or `deploy.resources.limits.memory: 6g`, `pids_limit: 512`. Confirm `git clone` and the CLIs still work without capabilities (they do not need any).

Re-run the acceptance checks from T-0165: `docker build --platform linux/amd64 ...` succeeds (record image size and four versions), `docker compose -f docker-compose.executor.yml config` validates with a dummy executor.env, ORCH_CREDS and ORCH_NET exported, no ports, exactly the six mounts (four creds, work, and the two config files), objective secret grep returns nothing. `uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green. Commit on the task branch. Finish with: summary, files changed, image size, versions, which downloads are checksum-verified, failures-only test output.
acceptance: protected-paths.txt names ~/orch-creds and the four container paths; the runbook uses the same default and tells how to protect a different root

compose joins an external network from ORCH_NET with a :? guard, guards ORCH_CREDS, defaults UID/GID, mounts repos.toml and pool.toml read-only from ./config, keeps no ports, adds no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL, a memory limit and pids_limit
Runbook order creates executor.env, ./work and ./config (chowned) before any compose run; explains network discovery and the config edit/restart flow and the target-repo pool.toml rule

Dockerfile pins the base image by digest and platform, selects the codex asset by architecture, verifies the codex tarball by checksum and records installer script hashes; a comment states what is verified
.dockerignore excludes .git, .mcp*.json, operator state under .orchestrator and config/; the image still builds with uv sync --frozen
Build and compose acceptance checks from T-0165 re-run and reported; objective secret grep clean; unit tests green; committed on the task branch; only the five scoped files change
